title: Kipper and orange pâté on toast

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Kippers, butter, crème fraîche, horseradish sauce, oranges and bread are all traditional household foods, with no factory-made products beyond a classic condiment.

supermarket.reason: Kipper fillets, oranges and the rest are everyday items at Tesco and similar shops, at ordinary prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a bowl, a fork and a frying pan, and soaking, flaking and mashing are simple techniques.

works.reason: Soaking the kippers in boiling water, mashing them into a pâté and toasting the bread gives a well-seasoned, generous snack for four, with peppery horseradish balancing the smoky fish and orange.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes is realistic for flaking, mashing, peeling the oranges and toasting, and the 5-minute cook matches the kipper soak.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and the pepper are used in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: February oranges appear as zest through the pâté and as a full topping of two sliced oranges, so they are a co-star rather than a garnish in a warming winter snack.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Oily fish on wholemeal toast with fresh fruit is a proper, nourishing snack a family would happily make again.
